title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is currently navigating a mix of new technology tests and strategic partnerships, while also grappling with the realities of hiring in a competitive landscape. Budget increases signal a focus on resilience, but the specter of delays in hypersonic testing looms large.

themes.title: Propulsion and Maneuverability Advances
themes.body: Parabilis is making strides with its propulsion system aimed at maneuverable cubesats, a niche that could redefine small satellite operations. This development highlights the ongoing push for more agile and responsive space capabilities.

themes.title: Budget Boost for Space Resilience
themes.body: The recent FY27 budget markup adds $1.4 billion to the space resilience line, underscoring a commitment to strengthening national security in orbit. This funding could catalyze innovative projects, but execution will be key.

themes.title: Commercial Space Consortium in China
themes.body: China's unveiling of its state-backed commercial space consortium reflects a strategic move to consolidate resources and expertise in the competitive global space market. The implications for international partnerships and competition are worth monitoring.

themes.title: Hiring Dilemmas in Space Sector
themes.body: As the space industry contemplates ambitious hiring plans, the challenge remains to balance growth with the legacy of established players. This tension could shape the workforce dynamics and innovation pace in the coming years.
